subject: R's Makeconf (bonus topic: -mtune config for Mac)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: R's Makeconf (bonus topic: -mtune config for Mac)
parts:
I just installed R 3.0.0 from the binary.

Then I tracked down where Makeconf is:

/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/etc/Makeconf

The optimization level there is -O2, so I must've set
it to -O0 myself at some point. D'Oh.

So I set it to -O3 in CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS and it didn't take
particularly long to install.

I also ntoiced that there's now a CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS option

-mtune=core2

which I tried to change it to

-mtune=corei7

for my i7 Macbook, but it wasn't recognized. Probably because
the Mac's gcc isn't up to date with the rest of the world.

Does anyone know what I should be using for my i7 Macbook? Here's
the gcc doc:

See: http://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/i386-and-x86_002d64-Options.html

- Bob

On Friday, May 17, 2013 1:33:38 AM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:
You could try -mtune=native.

Neither -mtune=corei7 (which is recognized for me) nor -mtune=native saved any time for test-unit. It might for the models, but my impression is that most of these optimizations are for atomic types and wouldn't affect the execution time of Stan much yet.

Ben

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: R's Makeconf (bonus topic: -mtune config for Mac)
parts:
In my experience, -mtune=native usually has only a small impact on
performance in the best of cases (unless it's compared to something
ridiculous like m-tune=x86 which effectively turns off SIMD
instructions). For large models which spend a lot of time in calls to
Eigen it might make a noticeable impact. At any rate, -mtune=native
is ideal for building stan models since the executable will only ever
run on the machine it's built on, so we should turn it on if possible.

Cheers,
Marcus
